rationale: P identifies the braking behavior that must be characterised to evaluate prevention of unintended braking. H-3 establishes unintended stopping as the hazardous event, and SG-3 directly makes unintended braking the target; braking behavior is therefore part of the phenomenon itself, not merely a control mechanism affecting it. The declared scope matches H-3, and P does not add sensing, computation, communication, failure-mitigation mechanisms, or their timing constraints.
determining_elements: “Braking behavior of the ego vehicle” directly addresses the behavior targeted by H-3 and SG-3.
“Whether braking occurs and whether it is intended or unintended” identifies the occurrence and character necessary to evaluate T.
The scope preserves H-3’s straight-ahead urban driving situation at 50 km/h, with no visible obstacles or vehicles ahead and good weather.
P remains focused on vehicle braking rather than expanding to the mechanisms that detect obstacles, generate commands, or mitigate failures.
